title: Old Creole songs, his brother, and Mardi Gras
summary: Picou says his brother composed Creole songs; they discuss titles and translations and playing them at Mardi Gras.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Were there any of the other old Creole songs that you could remember besides El Abado?
Oh, I know so much of them.
Did you ever play them on dance jobs?
Yeah.
Yeah? Yes, I did. Do you remember any of them that you used?
If my brother was living, and would be sitting right here now, he's the one that composed all Creole songs. Really? El Abado. What was his name? Eulis. Eulis. Eulis.
Uh-huh. Do you remember the names of any of the songs
that they used to have there? Oh, Gangnam. Who stole my bottle?
Who stole my bottle?
Who stole my bottle? No. No, wait. Who stole my bottle? Who told you I was going over there? That's cool. Oh, Lord, if I can think about him.
These were songs? Huh? These were songs?
Yeah.
I see.
And he had a voice, a light kind of voice. And when he sang, everybody keep going. He had a voice. Yeah. And I played with that in handy.
What does it mean in Creole? There was a song which was called, No Me Pa La Mesa. Huh?
No Me Pa La Mesa? That's him.
What is it?
What is it? I don't like that.
It means I don't like that. Yeah.
I don't like that.
I see.
That was a Mardi Gras song.
It was a Mardi Gras song? Yeah.
Oh. I see.
And you played it in Mardi Gras? Oh, sure. I mean, songs like that at Mardi Gras? Sure. I see.
Oh, yeah. It was all over. Oh, Lord. I had three, four jobs in one day. I didn't know why. I wish we'd have gone.
Yeah. Les soignons? Huh? Les soignons?
Les soignons? Yeah. Oui. It's a fish on the boat.
Uh-huh. What does that mean?
Oh, the onion is somewhat good.
Oh, is that nothing?
That's the translation.
I see.
